16 Sep 2023 · Letter · PsyArXiv (open letter); follow-up in Nature Neuroscience 28, 689-693 (2025)

The integrated information theory of consciousness as pseudoscience

IIT-Concerned, Fleming SM, Frith CD and others

A group of researchers called IIT pseudoscience, which set off a public dispute over what counts as a test of a theory of consciousness.

After press coverage called IIT a leading, tested theory, researchers wrote an open letter objecting. In 2025 a follow-up in Nature Neuroscience argued the theory's core claims cannot be tested even in principle. The row is about what a fair test of a theory of consciousness looks like.

Letter posted 16 Sep 2023 on PsyArXiv. Follow-up: IIT-Concerned et al., 'What makes a theory of consciousness unscientific?', Nature Neuroscience 28, 689-693, doi:10.1038/s41593-025-01881-x (104 author entries in Crossref, including the collective name). We did not verify the number of signatories on the 2023 letter.

What we do with it

It is why we judge every theory only by predictions sealed in advance. Planned

Read the original. Source checked against the original.
